issues.description: The problem specification and UML indicate that Animal.name is of type String, but the solution implementation declares the field as a StringBuilder. This is an attribute type mismatch: students reading the UML/description will expect to implement and interact with a String field, while the reference solution uses StringBuilder internally. This divergence can confuse students and may cause reflection-based checks or expectations about the field type to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal.name attribute type consistent with the UML/specification by using a String field instead of StringBuilder. For example, change the solution's field to 'private String name;', update the constructor to assign the String directly, and have the getter return the String (and setter accept a String). This preserves the intended design and avoids confusion or reflection-based test failures.
